newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Floods cut off Australian outback towns.
newsitem.headline: Floods cut off Australian outback towns.

text.p: Floodwaters isolated about 2,000 people in the Australian town of Wee Waa in New South Wales state on Monday, while heavy rain swelled rivers in other parts of outback Australia.
State emergency authorities said Wee Waa was likely to be cut off for about two days by the flooded Namoi River, which has also isolated about 20 rural properties.
"The waters have peaked at seven metres (23 feet) and the river's 30-40 km (19 to 25 miles) wide now, so there's extensive rural flooding," said State Emergency Services spokesman Bob Allen.
A helicopter has been sent to the town to check on outlying properties and evacuate residents if necessary.
The rainfall and flooding could take a toll on the region's cotton crop, with growers watching the weather anxiously ahead of the harvest starting next month.

The Gwydir and Namoi valleys in northern New South Wales produce about 40 percent of Australia's cotton crop, which is estimated to be worth a total of about A$1.1 billion ($840 million). In Queensland state, to the north, the town of Goondiwindi remained cut off after floodwaters rose around the town on Friday, but police said there were no plans for evacuations or food drops.
In South Australia state, the Australian air force prepared on Monday to drop 10 tonnes of food to residents stranded in the town of Oodnadatta, isolated by floods a week ago.
